```{=html}
<section class="hero">
  <img src="branding/akriti-mark-dark.svg" alt="Akriti" class="mark">
  <h1 class="wordmark">ĀKRITI</h1>
  <p class="backronym-tagline">Assured Knowledge &amp; Reasoning In Topological Inference</p>
  <p class="tagline">Statistically grounded topological data analysis for Python.</p>
  <p class="sublede">Persistence diagrams tell you what shape your data has. Akriti tells you whether the answer is <em>significant</em> — hypothesis tests, effect sizes, and sample-size calculation, with computation delegated to GUDHI and Ripser. Apache-2.0, open source, contributions welcome.</p>
  <div class="badges">
    <span class="badge primary">In development · first release 2026</span>
    <span class="badge">Apache-2.0</span>
    <span class="badge">Built on GUDHI &amp; Ripser</span>
  </div>
</section>
```

```{=html}
<section class="akriti-section" id="about">
  <div class="akriti-container">
    <h3 class="section-heading">About</h3>
    <h2 class="section-title">The statistical layer that Python's TDA stack is missing.</h2>
    <div class="about-grid">
      <div class="etymology">
        <div class="devanagari">आकृति</div>
        <div class="translit">ākṛti · Sanskrit, n.</div>
        <div class="gloss">The configurational form by which an instance is recognised as a member of its class.</div>
        <div class="backronym">
          <div class="backronym-label">AKRITI · backronym</div>
          <div class="backronym-expansion">
            <strong>A</strong>ssured <strong>K</strong>nowledge &amp;
            <strong>R</strong>easoning <strong>I</strong>n
            <strong>T</strong>opological <strong>I</strong>nference
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div>
        <p class="lede">A scientist who computes a persistence diagram is left holding a picture. The questions that follow are statistical ones — <em>is this feature significant? how large is the effect? how much data would I need to detect it?</em> — and in Python there has been nowhere to ask them. That tooling exists, but almost entirely in <strong>R</strong>. <strong>Akriti brings it to Python</strong>, and adds what neither language has: closed-form guarantees and a sample-size calculus for topological effects.</p>
        <p class="lede" style="font-size:16px;color:#444;">Akriti also answers the question that stops most newcomers cold — <em>which filtration, which scale, which dimension?</em> Where our theory supports a principled default, the library chooses and tells you why. Where it provably does not, the library says so and points you at cross-validation rather than pretending. Honest defaults, with guardrails.</p>
        <div class="ecosystem-line">
          Akriti sits on top of <code>GUDHI</code> and <code>Ripser</code> for persistence computation and integrates with the scientific Python ecosystem (<code>scikit-learn</code>, <code>AnnData</code>, <code>scanpy</code>). It does not replace existing tools; it makes them easier to use together.
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```

```{=html}
<section class="akriti-section" id="capabilities">
  <div class="akriti-container">
    <h3 class="section-heading">What Akriti does</h3>
    <h2 class="section-title">A toolkit, not a single trick.</h2>
    <p class="lede" style="font-size:15px;color:#555;">Akriti is early. Modules are marked <em>building</em> where work is under way and <em>planned</em> where they are on the roadmap — we would rather be accurate than impressive.</p>
    <div class="cap-grid">
      <div class="cap-card">
        <div class="cap-name">akriti.diagrams · <em>building</em></div>
        <div class="cap-title">One diagram format</div>
        <div class="cap-body">A single persistence-diagram type with adapters for GUDHI, Ripser, giotto-tda, persim, and plain arrays — so you never write conversion glue again. Useful even if you use nothing else here.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="cap-card">
        <div class="cap-name">akriti.castle · <em>building</em></div>
        <div class="cap-title">Statistics for diagrams</div>
        <div class="cap-body">A two-sample test with an effect size in bottleneck distance, a <strong>sample-size calculator</strong> for topological effects, a per-region significance map, and a robustness certificate — plus a reporting card you can paste into a methods section.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="cap-card">
        <div class="cap-name">akriti.core · <em>building</em></div>
        <div class="cap-title">Embeddings &amp; certificates</div>
        <div class="cap-body">The bi-Lipschitz landmark embeddings of PLACE and PALACE, closed-form descriptor selection with its validity conditions stated explicitly, and Pinelis / Gaussian certificate radii.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="cap-card">
        <div class="cap-name">akriti.compute · <em>planned</em></div>
        <div class="cap-title">Diagrams from data</div>
        <div class="cap-body">Vietoris–Rips, alpha, cubical, and sublevel-set filtrations on point clouds, images, time series, and graphs, with defaults chosen for you. Delegates to GUDHI and Ripser; we do not reimplement persistence.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="cap-card">
        <div class="cap-name">akriti.vectorise · <em>planned</em></div>
        <div class="cap-title">Embed for ML</div>
        <div class="cap-body">Persistence images, landscapes, Betti curves, and landmark embeddings — with a maintained benchmark comparing them, so you can choose on evidence rather than habit.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="cap-card">
        <div class="cap-name">akriti.compat · <em>planned</em></div>
        <div class="cap-title">A home for giotto-tda users</div>
        <div class="cap-body">giotto-tda has been unmaintained since 2024. A compatibility layer lets existing pipelines keep running, on maintained and permissively licensed code.</div>
      </div>
    </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```

```{=html}
<section class="akriti-section" id="stack">
  <div class="akriti-container">
    <h3 class="section-heading">Where Akriti fits</h3>
    <h2 class="section-title">A thin, statistical layer above the engines.</h2>
    <p class="lede">Akriti doesn't replace <a href="https://gudhi.inria.fr/">GUDHI</a> or <a href="https://ripser.scikit-tda.org/">Ripser</a> — it sits on top of them. They compute the persistence diagrams; Akriti decides what to compute, turns the result into a claim you can defend, and hands it on to scikit-learn or scanpy. Roughly the relationship <code>statsmodels</code> has with NumPy.</p>

    <div class="compare-closing">
      <p>Three gaps prompted Akriti, stated as precisely as we can:</p>
      <ol>
        <li><strong>Statistical inference for diagrams lives in R, not Python.</strong> The <code>TDA</code>, <code>TDAstats</code> and <code>tdaverse</code> packages have offered permutation tests and bootstrap confidence sets for years. Python users have had essentially nothing.</li>
        <li><strong>No library, in any language, calculates sample size for a topological effect.</strong> <em>"How many samples do I need to detect a bottleneck-distance difference of size δ?"</em> is a question applied statistics answers routinely, and topology has never answered at all.</li>
        <li><strong>Python's general-purpose TDA layer has gone quiet.</strong> giotto-tda has had no commits since 2024 while still being installed thousands of times a month. Its users deserve somewhere maintained to land.</li>
      </ol>
      <p>GUDHI is healthy, actively released, and the backend we depend on. Ripser, Hera, persim, scikit-tda and the R <code>tdaverse</code> are the shoulders this stands on. We ship a complement, not a replacement — and we would far rather interoperate than compete.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```

```{=html}
<section class="akriti-section" id="code">
  <div class="akriti-container">
    <h3 class="section-heading">In Python</h3>
    <h2 class="section-title">From diagram to defensible claim.</h2>
    <p class="lede">Bring diagrams from any backend, or let Akriti compute them. Either way you finish with a number you can put in a paper. <em>API shown is indicative and still settling.</em></p>
    <pre class="code-block"><span class="k">import</span> <span class="n">akriti</span>

<span class="c"># ── Bring diagrams from wherever you already compute them ─────</span>
<span class="n">D</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">akriti</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">diagrams</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">from_gudhi</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">st</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">persistence</span><span class="o">())</span>

<span class="c"># ── Are these two groups topologically different? ─────────────</span>
<span class="n">test</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">akriti</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">castle</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">two_sample</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">group_A</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">group_B</span><span class="o">)</span>
<span class="b">print</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">test</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">p_value</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">test</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">effect_size</span><span class="o">)</span>

<span class="c"># ── How much data would I have needed? ─────────────────────</span>
<span class="n">n</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">akriti</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">castle</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">sample_size</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">effect</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="m">0.1</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">power</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="m">0.8</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">pilot</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="n">D</span><span class="o">)</span>

<span class="c"># ── A reporting card for the methods section ────────────────</span>
<span class="b">print</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">test</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">report</span><span class="o">())</span></pre>
  </div>
</section>
```

```{=html}
<section class="akriti-section" id="research">
  <div class="akriti-container">
    <h3 class="section-heading">Founding research</h3>
    <h2 class="section-title">The papers behind the library.</h2>
    <p class="lede" style="font-size:15px;color:#555;">Akriti is grounded in four research papers from the founding team. CASTLE is the practitioner-facing product; the others are the machinery that makes its guarantees possible.</p>
    <div class="papers-grid">
      <div class="paper-card">
        <div class="tag">PLACE · Paper I</div>
        <div class="title">A Closed-Form Persistence-Landmark Pipeline for Certified Point-Cloud and Graph Classification</div>
        <div class="meta">TMLR · 2026 (under review)</div>
      </div>
      <div class="paper-card">
        <div class="tag">PALACE · Paper II</div>
        <div class="title">Adaptive Landmark Embeddings for Persistence Diagrams: Closed-Form Mahalanobis Selection and Per-Prediction Certificates</div>
        <div class="meta">JMLR · 2026 (under review)</div>
      </div>
      <div class="paper-card">
        <div class="tag">Paper III</div>
        <div class="title">A Statistical-Inference Pipeline for Persistence-Landmark Kernels: CLT, Berry–Esseen, and Functional Limits</div>
        <div class="meta">In preparation · 2026</div>
      </div>
      <div class="paper-card">
        <div class="tag">CASTLE · Paper IV</div>
        <div class="title">A Practitioner's Toolkit for Topological Two-Sample Testing, Sample-Size Calculation, and Robustness Certification</div>
        <div class="meta">In preparation · 2026</div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="built-on">
      <h4>Built on</h4>
      <p>Akriti delegates persistence computation to <a href="https://gudhi.inria.fr/">GUDHI</a> (INRIA) and <a href="https://ripser.scikit-tda.org/">Ripser</a>, and builds on the landmark embedding of <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.04860">Mitra &amp; Virk (2024)</a>. We are grateful to the broader topological data analysis community — <a href="https://giotto-ai.github.io/gtda-docs/">giotto-tda</a>, <a href="https://persim.scikit-tda.org/">persim</a>, <a href="https://ripser.scikit-tda.org/">ripser.py</a>, the R <a href="https://github.com/tdaverse">tdaverse</a>, and the many inference, vectorisation and stability results the library stands on.</p>
      <p style="margin-top:12px;color:#666;font-size:13px;"><em>A "Publications using Akriti" section will appear here as case studies are published.</em></p>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```
